questions.text:
Directions:

Which of the following symbols should be placed in the question mark (?) respectively (in the same order from left to right) in order to complete the given expression in such a manner that “N < S” is definitely true and “R > O” is false.

Statement: M < N ≤ O; P ? Q ; S > R ≥ Q ; P = O
questions.explanation:
Statement: M < N ≤ O; P ? Q ; S > R ≥ Q ; P = O
On combining: M < N ≤ O = P ? Q ≤ R < S
Options:
1)= → M < N ≤ O = P = Q ≤ R < S → True (N < S → definitely true; R > O→ Hence we don’t have clear relation between R and O. R can be greater or equal to O,  R > O is false )
2)< → M < N ≤ O = P < Q ≤ R < S → False (N < S → definitely true; R > O →definitely true)
3)≤ → M < N ≤ O = P ≤ Q ≤ R < S → True (N < S → definitely true; R > O → Hence we don’t have clear relation between R and O. R can be greater or equal to O,  R > O is false )
Hence, either = or ≤ is the correct option.

questions.text: Which of the following expression is definitely true if the given expression 'P ≥ R' and 'V > S' are to be definitely true?

options.text: P = Q  ≥ R > S = T ≤ U < V
Q = P ≤ S = T < U < R ≤ V
V < S = T > U < R > P =Q
P < Q < R > S > T = U < V

questions.explanation:
Given Expression: 'P ≥ R' and 'V > S'

1) P = Q  ≥ R > S = T ≤ U < V → True (as P = Q  ≥ R → P ≥ R and S = T ≤ U < V → V > S)

2) Q = P ≤ S = T < U < R ≤ V → False (as P ≤ S = T < U < R → R > P)

3) V < S = T > U < R > P =Q → False (R > P)

4) P < Q < R > S > T = U < V → False (P < Q < R → R > P)

Hence, only expression 1 is true.
